title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
layout_note: The prior method and the proposed one are stacked rather than side by side: a one-line chain-of-thought (greedy decode) row on top, a grey dashed horizontal rule, then the self-consistency row taking about three quarters of the height, where one language-model box fans out into three sampled reasoning paths that converge on one final answer.
grouping: A grey dashed horizontal rule separates the two methods, each named by a bold row label at left ('Chain-of-thought prompting', 'Self-consistency'). A blue dashed rectangle encloses the three sampled reasoning texts.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with thin dark outlines, no shadows: white for the prompt, light grey for the language model, pale red or pale green for outputs; each sampled path is one box split into a reasoning-text cell and an answer cell. Connectors are thin grey curved lines; a hollow outlined block arrow points down from the top row's prompt to the full prompt below.
proposed_highlight: The bottom row is the larger part of the figure; its two new steps are named in blue bold text with blue dashed marks (a dashed box round the sampled paths, a dashed arrow to the final answer), and the aggregated answer is the only saturated fill (darker green).
lesson: Show sample-then-vote as geometry: one model box fans out into several quoted outputs whose answers sit in one aligned column, and their lines converge on a single darker answer box.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF's first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023'). The automatic crop (bbox top 82.6 pt) cut off the blue 'Greedy decode' label above the top row; the card was written from a hand-fixed crop with the box top at 74.0 pt, recorded in fetch.bbox_pt.

taxonomy.task: LLM reasoning by sampling several chain-of-thought paths and voting on the answer
taxonomy.note: family other: LLM prompting / decoding-time reasoning; architecture other: no network drawn, only a language-model box queried by a prompt

insights.structure: Prior method above a dashed rule as one short Prompt -> Language model -> output -> answer row; the proposed method below with the same order but three parallel output rows between the model and one final answer.
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are quoted verbatim: the full few-shot prompt in a tall white box and each reasoning path as its own text, with the answer split off into a bold cell at the right of each path.
insights.emphasis: New steps are named in blue bold labels with blue dashed marks, and the aggregated answer is the only darker-green fill; path colours mark answers that agree (green) or not (red).
insights.flow: Thin grey curves fan out from the language model to the three paths and converge from their answer cells onto the final answer; a hollow block arrow drops from the top prompt to the bottom prompt to say the same prompt is reused.
insights.avoid: The marginalisation step is a blue dashed annotation arrow that leaves the dashed box, loops up past the label and comes down onto the answer, a detour that duplicates the converging grey lines.

arrangement.units: two unframed rows separated by a grey dashed horizontal rule, each named by a bold label at the left; the lower row about three times the height of the upper
arrangement.inputs_as: a one-word 'Prompt' box in the top row; the full quoted few-shot prompt (Q/A exemplars and the test question) in a tall rounded box in the bottom row
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn (training-free); the vote is drawn as converging lines into the final answer box at the right
arrangement.shared: the language model is drawn once per row as an identical grey box; the shared prompt is linked across rows by a hollow downward block arrow

core.what: greedy chain-of-thought as one red path in a short row above a dashed rule, against self-consistency below, where three sampled paths fan out from the same model box and converge on one green answer

relations.form: the two methods stacked in rows with the same left-to-right order (prompt, language model, reasoning, answer), separated by a grey dashed rule, ours below and larger
three sampled reasoning paths stacked as equal-width two-cell boxes (reasoning | answer), their answer cells aligned in one column
thin curved lines from the three answer cells converge on a single darker-green 'The answer is $18.' box at the right
prompt -> language model -> outputs -> answer along one horizontal axis in each row

channels.colour: output fill = whether the path's answer agrees with the majority (pale green $18) or not (pale red $14, $26), darker green = the aggregated answer; blue = annotation of the new steps (labels and dashed marks); grey = the language model
channels.shape: rounded rectangles throughout: white = prompt input, grey = model, tinted = generated text; a split box = one sampled path with its answer cell
channels.line: thin grey curves = data flow; blue dashed = annotation (grouping box and the 'marginalize' arrow); grey dashed rule = separator between methods; hollow block arrow = the same prompt reused
channels.frame: a blue dashed rectangle = the set of sampled reasoning paths

quality.strengths: the fan-out from one model box into three paths and their convergence on one darker answer makes sample-then-vote readable before any label; data is drawn as real quoted prompt and reasoning text; answers are split into their own aligned column so the vote's inputs line up; the proposed row gets most of the area while the prior method is a compact single row
quality.weaknesses: the two rows do not align: the top prompt is a one-word box while the bottom quotes the prompt in full, so the two language-model boxes sit at different x positions and the shared steps cannot be compared column by column; the 'marginalize' step is a looping blue dashed annotation wire rather than an aggregation node; the quoted few-shot prompt fills the left third of the lower row, more space than the step it represents

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
